plain_idea.one_liner: Use recorded brain activity from speech-motor cortex to predict the words a paralysed person is trying to say.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need per-attempted-sentence neural recordings (electrode array firing rates over time) paired with the intended sentence. This paper provides none; number of examples is unknown because no file exists.
plain_idea.predict: The intended text or synthesised voice, scored against the sentence the participant was cued to say. That ground truth comes from the experimenter's cue script in the original brain-computer interface experiments, which are not this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Speech neuroprosthesis groups (UC Davis, Stanford BrainGate, UC San Francisco) would use better decoders directly, but nothing here supports building one — the usable data lives in the primary research articles and their separate public releases, not in this commentary.

ml_idea: None available from this item. Any speech-decoding project would have to be built on the primary research articles instead (for example the publicly released Brain-to-Text benchmark data from the Stanford/BrainGate intracortical speech work), evaluated as its own candidate.
